papers.title: Molecular determinants of ligand recognition and efficacy in the TRPM3 voltage sensor-like domain.
papers.abstract: Transient receptor potential melastatin 3 (TRPM3) is a calcium-permeable ion channel implicated in chronic pain and developmental and epileptic encephalopathies. The voltage sensor-like domain (VSLD) is a major site of pharmacological modulation, but the molecular determinants of ligand recognition and efficacy remain incompletely understood. Here we combine cryo-electron microscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, mutagenesis, and medicinal chemistry to investigate the interactions of TRPM3 with the inhibitors isosakuranetin, maprotiline, and diclofenac. We show that structurally diverse liga
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how structurally diverse inhibitors (isosakuranetin, maprotiline, and diclofenac) bind to the voltage sensor-like domain of the TRPM3 ion channel, a target for chronic pain and epilepsy. By combining cryo-electron microscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, mutagenesis, and medicinal chemistry, the authors identify key molecular determinants of ligand recognition and efficacy. The findings could guide the design of more selective TRPM3-targeting drugs.

papers.title: Design and Evolution of an Orthogonal HaloTag for Multiplexed Labeling in Cells.
papers.abstract: The self-labeling protein HaloTag is used to install a wide variety of functional small molecules in cells and living organisms with exquisite specificity with respect to cell type and subcellular localization. HaloTag is a core part of many biotechnology-based tools for sensing, tracking, and manipulating biological systems with a high degree of spatial and temporal control. Due to the limitations of fluorescent proteins and other self-labeling proteins, most of these tools have historically been restricted to a single channel. In this work, we used structure-guided rational design and direct
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors used structure-guided rational design and directed evolution to create an orthogonal HaloTag variant that can be labeled independently from the original HaloTag. This enables multiplexed labeling of two distinct protein populations in cells, expanding the utility of self-labeling tags for simultaneous sensing, tracking, and manipulation experiments.

papers.title: What deep learning can and cannot (yet) do for enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Deep learning has substantially advanced structure-based enzyme design, yet reliably creating highly efficient enzymes remains out of reach. One emerging enzyme design strategy combines diffusion-based scaffold generation around active-site models with sequence design. Such structure-based approaches have expanded the accessible reaction space and enabled the emergence of enzymes with diverse catalytic functions and complex catalytic motifs. Despite notable catalytic efficiencies (kcat/KM), turnover rates (kcat) often remain limited, suggesting that current approaches typically yield tight sub
papers.summary: This review examines the current capabilities and limitations of deep learning for enzyme design, highlighting that while diffusion-based scaffold generation combined with sequence design has expanded accessible reaction space and produced enzymes with diverse catalytic functions, reliably achieving high catalytic efficiency remains elusive. The key bottleneck is that while catalytic efficiencies (kcat/KM) can be notable, turnover rates (kcat) often remain limited, suggesting current approaches typically yield tight substrate binding but poor product release.

papers.title: Integrative proteomic analysis and molecular dynamics simulations of ANKLE2 reveal mechanisms of microcephaly.
papers.abstract: ANKLE2 is a scaffolding protein with crucial roles in neuroprogenitor cell division and embryonic brain development. Pathogenic variants in ANKLE2 cause primary microcephaly, a congenital disorder characterized by impaired neurodevelopment. Nonetheless, the underlying dysfunction of ANKLE2 is not understood. Here, we define the ANKLE2 protein interaction landscape, which includes cell division proteins and novel microcephaly candidates in the APC (anaphase-promoting complex). Analysis of six pathogenic variants reveals changes in this interactome that likely result in microcephaly. Using molec
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study maps the protein interaction network of ANKLE2, a scaffolding protein essential for neuroprogenitor division and brain development, identifying interactions with cell division machinery including the anaphase-promoting complex (APC). By combining proteomics with molecular dynamics simulations across six pathogenic variants, the authors show how microcephaly-causing mutations disrupt these interactions, offering mechanistic insight into the disease.

papers.title: MHC restriction is structurally encoded by the T cell receptor germline.
papers.abstract: MHC restriction - the requirement for αβ T cell receptors (TCRs) to recognize Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) molecules when presenting peptide antigens - is a pillar of adaptive immunity. Here, we provide direct structural evidence for TCR germline-encoded recognition of MHC molecules irrespective of antigenic peptide. We engineered "germline-like" TCRs to eliminate CDR3 specificity for peptide, and a molecular clamping strategy to trap ultra-low-affinity complexes with peptide-MHC for cryo-EM. We find that germline-like TCR/pMHC docking modes are identical to wild-type T cell receptor
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study provides direct structural evidence that T cell receptors recognize MHC molecules through germline-encoded features, independent of the specific peptide antigen. By engineering germline-like TCRs and using a molecular clamping strategy to trap ultra-low-affinity complexes for cryo-EM, the authors show that germline-like TCR/pMHC docking modes are identical to wild-type TCRs. This supports the long-standing hypothesis that MHC restriction is structurally encoded in the TCR germline.

papers.title: Syndirella: synthesis-directed fragment elaboration enables extensive and cost-effective binding site exploration beyond catalog compounds.
papers.abstract: Fragment screens provide an information-rich starting point for designing derivative compounds in structure-based drug discovery. However, derivatives in the fragment-to-hit stage are typically designed from only one or a few fragments, risking premature convergence on an unproductive series and dramatically limiting exploration of the binding site's interaction opportunities. This is avoidable by exploring a broad, chemically diverse set of scaffolds and elaborations spanning interactions revealed across many fragments, as well as those not yet observed. Conventional catalog procurement makes
papers.summary: Syndirella is a computational tool that designs diverse derivative compounds from many fragment hits rather than just one or two, enabling broader exploration of a binding site's interaction opportunities in fragment-to-hit drug discovery. By synthesizing compounds on demand instead of relying on catalog procurement, it offers a cost-effective way to probe chemical space beyond what is commercially available.

papers.title: Single-Particle STORM Imaging Quantifies Coating Heterogeneity Among Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoparticles.
papers.abstract: Cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (CNPs) are a potentially transformative biomimetic targeted-delivery platform, which can engage therapeutic targets through source-cell membrane protein functions or homotypic interactions. However, their therapeutic development is limited by the current inability to accurately resolve membrane coating completeness, and CNP particle-to-particle variation. Here, we introduce a STochastic Optical Reconstruction Microscopy (STORM)-based approach that resolves population composition and quantifies membrane coating coverage at the single-particle level. Applying i
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces a STORM-based super-resolution imaging method to quantify how completely individual cell membrane-coated nanoparticles are covered by their membrane coating, resolving particle-to-particle heterogeneity that was previously invisible. This matters because incomplete or variable coatings limit the therapeutic reliability of these biomimetic delivery platforms.

papers.title: Microbial aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase degrades metformin to limit therapeutic response in type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Metformin is a first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes, yet therapeutic responses vary widely. Whether gut microbes directly inactivate metformin and limit its efficacy remains unclear. Here, we identify a gut microbial aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase, AdhE, from Eubacterium species enriched in individuals with a low response to metformin. AdhE converts metformin to pharmacologically inactive products, lowering intestinal and systemic drug exposure. Genetic deletion of AdhE or phage-mediated depletion of AdhE-producing Eubacterium hallii MD1 restores metformin exposure and glycemic control in mi
papers.summary: This study identifies a gut microbial enzyme, aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase (AdhE), from Eubacterium species that inactivates metformin by converting it into pharmacologically inactive products, thereby reducing drug exposure and limiting its therapeutic efficacy in type 2 diabetes. Deleting AdhE or depleting AdhE-producing E. hallii MD1 via phage restores metformin levels and improves glycemic control in mice. The findings reveal a direct microbial mechanism underlying variable metformin responses and suggest targeting gut bacteria as a strategy to enhance therapy.

papers.title: Fixed Nonsynonymous vOka Vaccine Mutations in IE62 drive Varicella-Zoster Virus Attenuation in Human Skin.
papers.abstract: The live, attenuated vaccine for Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV) protects against chickenpox in children and adults. However, the vaccine strain Oka (vOka) establishes latency and may reactivate. The molecular basis of vOka attenuation remains unknown. We investigated whether three high-frequency single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that differentiate vOka from parental strain Oka (pOka) are responsible: S628G and R958G in the immediate-early regulatory protein IE62, and *130R in the membrane protein ORF0. We evaluated how these fixed SNPs mediate the attenuated growth phenotype of VZV and dimi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study identifies three fixed nonsynonymous mutations that distinguish the attenuated varicella-zoster vaccine strain (vOka) from its parental strain, focusing on two mutations in the IE62 regulatory protein and one in ORF0. Using human skin models, the authors show that the IE62 mutations (S628G and R958G) are key drivers of the vaccine's attenuated growth phenotype. These findings provide a molecular explanation for how the live vaccine is weakened while retaining its ability to establish latency.

papers.title: A de novo GABPA Variant in a Patient with Multifocal Cutaneous Vascular Tumors of an Unclassified Entity.
papers.abstract: We investigated the genetic basis of a previously unclassified congenital vascular anomaly in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors. Through genomic analysis, we identified a novel heterozygous de novo germline variant in GA-binding protein-alpha (GABPA), an ETS family transcription factor. Histopathologic evaluation demonstrated capillary-venous lesions lacking glucose transporter 1 expression, distinguishing this entity from common infantile hemangioma. Notably, the tumor vasculature exhibited a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular cell layer, with nuclear localized GABPA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This case study identifies a novel de novo germline variant in the GABPA transcription factor in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors that do not fit any known classification. The tumors lacked GLUT1 expression, distinguishing them from infantile hemangioma, and showed a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular layer with nuclear GABPA localization. The finding suggests GABPA dysfunction may drive a previously unrecognized vascular tumor entity.

papers.title: A water-pinning hotspot drives templated tau aggregation.
papers.abstract: Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP), achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured sol
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how tau, an intrinsically disordered protein, forms seed-competent fibrils that propagate between cells in neurodegenerative tauopathies. The authors identify a single dominant 'water-pinning' hotspot that drives in-register stacking of tau monomers onto fibril templates, preventing mismatched aggregation. This mechanism may explain the templated, prion-like spread of tau pathology.

papers.title: GeoEPred: A multimodal structure-aware geometric deep learning framework for Gram-negative bacterial secreted effector prediction with sequence semantics.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria is important for elucidating bacterial pathogenic mechanisms and developing precise anti-infective strategies. Although existing methods have benefited from the strong sequence feature extraction capacity of pretrained protein language models, reliance on linear sequence information alone often fails to fully capture the three-dimensional conformational signals required for virulence functions. Meanwhile, conventional structure-based methods are limited by the scarcity of experimentally resolved protein structures. To
papers.summary: GeoEPred is a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts secreted effector proteins in Gram-negative bacteria by combining protein language model sequence embeddings with geometric features derived from predicted 3D structures. This structure-aware approach aims to overcome the limitations of sequence-only methods and the scarcity of experimental structures, potentially improving effector identification for understanding bacterial pathogenesis.

papers.title: Synthesis, Moleculer Modeling, and Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitor Effects of Novel 1-(1-benzyl-2-oxoindolin-3-ylidene)-4-(3-sulfamoylphenyl)thiosemicarbazides.
papers.abstract: In this study, we describe the synthesis of new 1-(1-benzyl-2-oxoindolin-3-ylidene)-4-(3-sulfamoylphenyl)thiosemicarbazides and evaluate their inhibitory activity against hCAs (6a-l). The inhibitory effects of compounds 6a-l were examined in vitro against hCA I, II, IX, and XII isoforms. Acetazolamide (AAZ) was employed as the standard reference compound in this study. The compounds 6a-l inhibited the tumor-associated hCA IX and XII isoenzymes at nanomolar levels, and showed weak inhibitory effects on the off-target hCA I and II isoenzymes. Selectivity index (SI) values of compounds 6a-l were
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of novel thiosemicarbazide compounds and tested their ability to inhibit different carbonic anhydrase (CA) enzymes. The compounds showed potent nanomolar inhibition of the tumor-associated hCA IX and XII isoforms while having weak effects on off-target hCA I and II, suggesting potential for selective anticancer activity.

papers.title: Capturing Hu Antigen R Domain Closure Through Supervised Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Hu antigen R (HuR), an RNA-binding protein implicated in cancer, inflammation, and neurodegenerative disorders, represents a challenging target for drug discovery due to its large solvent-exposed RNA-binding interface and pronounced conformational flexibility. HuR contains tandem RNA recognition motifs (RRM1 and RRM2) that undergo substantial rearrangements between an apo open state and an RNA-bound closed conformation. Here, we investigated both states using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. While the RNA-bound complex maintained a stable closed architecture, the apo form displayed extensi
papers.summary: This study uses supervised molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the conformational transition of the RNA-binding protein HuR between its open apo state and closed RNA-bound state. The simulations reveal that the RNA-bound complex remains stable in a closed architecture, while the apo form exhibits extensive flexibility, providing mechanistic insight into a challenging drug target. This work may inform future efforts to design inhibitors that trap or stabilize specific HuR conformations.

papers.title: Molecular insights into the selective interaction of endocrine-disrupting chemicals with poly(mannuronate) in aqueous systems: a multiscale computational study.
papers.abstract: Estrogens and other steroid hormones, also known as endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), are emerging contaminants in wastewater effluent due to human activities. Although these compounds play essential roles in medical treatments and modern agriculture, their release into the environment has raised concerns because of their potential ecological and health impacts. The selective removal of EDCs from aqueous environments is a challenge due to competition with water molecules for binding sites. This work presents a systematic computational investigation of the intermolecular interactions and p
papers.summary: This computational study investigates how endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) such as estrogens selectively bind to poly(mannuronate), a polysaccharide found in brown algae, in aqueous environments. Using multiscale modeling, the authors characterize the intermolecular interactions that allow these pollutants to be captured despite competition from water molecules. The findings could inform the design of bio-based adsorbents for removing EDCs from wastewater.

papers.title: Design and in silico evaluation of PV-GNProtecta: an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis.
papers.abstract: Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population coverage analysis suggested broad HLA
papers.summary: This study uses immunoinformatics and structural analysis to design an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate, PV-GNProtecta, against Puumala virus, targeting conserved regions of its glycoprotein and nucleoprotein. The authors identified antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes, combined them with adjuvants, and predicted broad HLA population coverage. The work is entirely computational (in silico), so experimental validation of immunogenicity and protection remains to be done.

papers.title: Integrative pan-cancer analysis of AKT1 and structure-based drug design by buckwheat derived compounds.
papers.abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Sheikh et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. AKT1 is a serine-threonine protein-kinase involved in tumour cell proliferation, survival, metabolism, and therapeutic resistance via activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. However, the comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of AKT1 and systematics identifications of natural AKT1 inhibitors remains limited. T
papers.summary: This study performs a pan-cancer analysis of AKT1, a kinase central to the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, to characterize its role across tumor types. The authors then use structure-based drug design to identify buckwheat-derived natural compounds as potential AKT1 inhibitors. The work aims to bridge comprehensive cancer genomics with natural product drug discovery targeting AKT1.

papers.title: Large-scale prospective evaluation of co-folding across hundreds of Mac1-ligand complexes and three virtual screens.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of ligand-bound protein complexes and ranking them by affinity are central problems in drug discovery. While deep-learning co-folding methods can help address these challenges, their evaluation has been hampered by the difficulties in assessing independence from training data and insufficiently large test sets. Here, we test the ability of co-folding methods to predict the structures of 551 ligands, 489 of which are of sufficient quality for evaluation, bound to the SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 macrodomain (Mac1) that were determined after the training cutoff dates. AlphaFold3 (AF3), Bo
papers.summary: This study prospectively evaluates deep-learning co-folding methods on 489 Mac1-ligand complexes determined after training cutoffs, testing both structure prediction and virtual screening performance. It provides a rigorous, large-scale benchmark that addresses common concerns about training data contamination in co-folding model evaluation.

papers.title: Transforming the Landscape of Drug Innovation in AI Era: AlphaFold 3 and Beyond.
papers.abstract: The traditional drug discovery and development (DDD) pipeline has long been characterized by inefficiency and high costs. The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI), especially AI-based toolkits for protein structure and interaction prediction, exemplified by AlphaFold 3 (AF3), promises to reshape the landscape of drug innovation. AF3 advances structural biology by predicting protein structures and their interactions with a range of biomolecules, including nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, and ions, potentially changing the conventional DDD paradigm, although prediction accuracy
papers.summary: This review discusses how AI-based protein structure and interaction prediction tools, particularly AlphaFold 3, are reshaping the drug discovery and development pipeline. AF3 extends beyond protein structure prediction to model interactions with nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, and ions, potentially transforming the traditional costly and inefficient DDD paradigm, though accuracy limitations remain.

papers.title: PrOMet: Accurate and Robust Metal-Binding Site and Type Prediction.
papers.abstract: Metal binding to proteins is crucial for many biological functions, yet the prediction of metal-binding sites and metal types remains underexplored compared to other biomolecular interactions. Despite advances in deep learning, computational methods have achieved limited success in this area; even the best-reported approaches reach only moderate localization accuracy on high-resolution crystal structures, and even worse when applied to medium-resolution data. We hypothesize that the main challenge lies in the nature of metal binding. While the putative sites span the entire protein surface, ac
papers.summary: PrOMet is a new deep learning method for predicting where metals bind on proteins and which metal type binds there. It addresses a gap where existing tools perform poorly, especially on lower-resolution structures, by better modeling the fact that potential binding sites are spread across the whole protein surface. The method claims improved accuracy and robustness compared to prior approaches.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: This study uses the antifungal protein NFAP2 from Aspergillus fischeri as a guide to identify fungus-specific protein targets in Candida albicans, then applies structure-based drug repurposing to find existing compounds that hit those targets. The approach aims to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging drugs with known safety profiles against a pathogen with limited treatment options and rising resistance.

papers.title: Atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from Escherichia coli by cryo-EM and solid-state NMR.
papers.abstract: Mechanosensitive channels are central to cellular responses to membrane tension, yet the structural basis of their gating remains incompletely understood. Here, we determine the structures of wild-type and Gly22→Ser (G22S) mutants of MscL from Escherichia coli (EcMscL) by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) in peptide-based lipid nanodiscs and complement them with solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements in liposomes to capture their dynamics in a native-like membrane environment. The cryo-EM structures reveal a closed conformation, whereas analysis of the low-threshold G2
papers.summary: This study combines cryo-EM and solid-state NMR to determine the atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from E. coli in lipid nanodiscs and liposomes. The cryo-EM structures capture a closed conformation, while NMR reveals dynamic features in a native-like membrane, providing insight into the structural basis of mechanosensitive gating.

papers.title: In vivo fate-guided design of efficient delivery systems for PROTACs: from molecular rationales to clinical progress.
papers.abstract: Despite two decades of intensive molecular engineering, the clinical translation of proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) remains constrained by a fundamental paradox: high in vitro potency often fails to translate into in vivo efficacy due to poor pharmacokinetics (PK)/pharmacodynamics (PD) profiles and uncontrolled biodistribution. This review departs from conventional narratives centered on potency by introducing a framework focused on drug fate that explicitly connects the absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion (ADME), and tumor targeting of PROTACs with the rational design of
papers.summary: This review argues that the clinical translation of PROTACs has been limited not by potency but by poor drug fate—specifically ADME properties and uncontrolled biodistribution. It proposes a framework linking pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and tumor targeting to the rational design of delivery systems, and surveys progress toward clinical application.

papers.title: Fluorination: A strategy to tune the interactions of molecules and nanoscale systems with biological matter.
papers.abstract: Fluorination has become a key molecular engineering strategy in medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine, enabling the fine tuning of the physicochemical and biological properties of therapeutic molecules and drug delivery systems. The unique characteristics of fluorine, including its small steric footprint, high electronegativity, and exceptional strength of the C-F bond, enhance metabolic stability, modulate lipophilicity and acidity, and improve pharmacokinetic profiles. Beyond these well-established effects, fluorination has emerged as a tool for controlling the assembly and biological behavio
papers.summary: This review discusses how fluorination—adding fluorine atoms to molecules and nanoscale systems—can be used to tune their interactions with biological matter. It highlights how fluorine's unique properties (small size, high electronegativity, strong C-F bonds) improve metabolic stability, lipophilicity, acidity, and pharmacokinetics, and increasingly enable control over molecular assembly and biological behavior.

papers.title: DyME: An MD-based engine exploiting HTP mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry.
papers.abstract: Protein recognition mimicry is of great interest in the field of molecular bioengineering and rational design, with mutagenesis frequently employed to analyze the effects of altering amino acids involved in molecular recognition. The conformational and energetic effects of such alterations can be investigated in detail with the help of molecular dynamics (MD) methodologies. While existing MD-based computational tools can be used to explore a particular set of mutations at a time, suitable for small-scale studies, high-throughput (HTP) exploration of protein recognition for engineering purposes
papers.summary: DyME is a molecular dynamics-based engine designed to enable high-throughput exploration of protein mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry. It addresses the limitation of existing MD tools that can only handle small sets of mutations at a time, allowing larger-scale screening of how amino acid changes affect molecular recognition.

papers.title: Semi-Rational Design of CpNampt Mutants for Enhanced Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) Synthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.abstract: β-Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) serves as a direct precursor of the essential cofactor NAD⁺, playing a crucial role in regulating mitochondrial function and delaying cellular aging. Synthetic biology, with its environmental and economic advantages, has become an important approach for the production of natural medicines, with the optimized design of metabolic pathways at its core. In this study, we focused on the NMN‑consuming pathway mediated by the nma1 and pof1 genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and consequently generated their double‑knockout mutant, DHSX02. Futhermore, a highly efficie
papers.summary: This study engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae to boost production of β-nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), a precursor to the anti-aging cofactor NAD⁺, by knocking out the NMN-consuming genes nma1 and pof1 and semi-rationally designing mutants of the CpNampt enzyme. The resulting strains improved NMN synthesis, demonstrating a synthetic biology approach to producing this valuable nutraceutical compound.

papers.title: The PTPN1/N2 Peptide Inhibitor Achieves Potent, Long-Acting Glycemic Control and Weight-Loss Dual Efficacy in Mice.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity are closely linked metabolic disorders driven by insulin and leptin resistance. Current long-acting therapies capable of addressing both conditions are dominated by incretin-based agents, which primarily achieve efficacy through appetite suppression and are frequently associated with tolerability limitations and metabolic rebound after treatment discontinuation. Alternative strategies that correct underlying signaling defects without suppressing food intake remain lacking. Protein tyrosine phosphatases PTPN1 and PTPN2 act as coordinated intracellular negati
papers.summary: This study reports a peptide inhibitor targeting PTPN1 and PTPN2 that simultaneously improves blood glucose control and promotes weight loss in mice. Unlike incretin-based drugs that mainly work by suppressing appetite, this approach corrects underlying insulin and leptin signaling defects, offering a potentially more durable dual-action therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity.

papers.title: ParaEM: Antigen-aware sequence-based paratope prediction with Expectation-Maximization.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of antibody paratopes-the residues contacting the antigen-is vital for understanding antibody-antigen recognition, antibody engineering, and vaccine design. However, structure-based predictors require antibody structural inputs, which are often obtained from experimentally determined antibody-antigen complexes in benchmark settings but are generally unavailable for new sequences. Conversely, sequence-based predictors scale efficiently but remain largely antigen-agnostic, limiting their use of pair-specific antigen context.
papers.summary: ParaEM is a new sequence-based method for predicting antibody paratopes (the residues that contact antigen) that incorporates antigen context using an Expectation-Maximization framework. Unlike prior sequence-based predictors that are largely antigen-agnostic, ParaEM leverages pair-specific antigen information, improving paratope prediction without requiring antibody structural inputs.

papers.title: Rational design of a consensus bothropic metalloproteinase as an immunogen for broadly protective antivenom development.
papers.abstract: Antivenoms remain the only specific therapy for snakebite envenoming. In Bothrops venoms, Snake Venom Metalloproteinases (SVMPs) are abundant and highly diverse toxins responsible for the major local and hemotoxic effects induced by envenoming. However, currently available bothropic antivenoms fail to fully neutralize these effects, frequently resulting in permanent and disabling sequelae in affected patients. Here, we describe a rational approach to improve the SVMP neutralization potential of bothropic antivenoms using a consensus toxin. Forty SVMP sequences belonging to PI, P-II, and P-III
papers.summary: The authors rationally designed a consensus snake venom metalloproteinase (SVMP) sequence based on 40 Bothrops SVMP sequences from the PI, P-II, and P-III classes, aiming to create a broadly immunogenic antigen. This consensus toxin is intended as an immunogen to elicit antivenom antibodies capable of neutralizing the diverse SVMPs responsible for local and hemotoxic damage in snakebite envenoming. The approach seeks to overcome the limited efficacy of current bothropic antivenoms against these highly variable toxins.

papers.title: Optimization of enzymatic hydrolysis for generating potential multifunctional peptides from goat milk: Bioactivity evaluation, structural characterization and molecular interaction analysis.
papers.abstract: Food-derived bioactive peptides have attracted increasing interest for functional food development. In this study, goat milk proteins were enzymatically hydrolyzed to generate peptides with inhibitory activities against α-glucosidase (α-G), dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV), and xanthine oxidase (XO). Protease screening and response surface methodology were applied to optimize the composite hydrolysis process. The optimized goat milk hydrolysate exhibited inhibitory activities of 73.05 ± 1.38%, 88.63 ± 2.76%, and 80.69 ± 1.65% against α-G, DPP-IV, and XO, respectively. The active peptide fracti
papers.summary: This study optimized enzymatic hydrolysis of goat milk proteins to produce bioactive peptides with inhibitory activity against three enzymes (α-glucosidase, DPP-IV, and xanthine oxidase), achieving inhibition rates of 73-89%. The researchers used protease screening and response surface methodology to optimize the process, then characterized the active peptide fractions structurally and analyzed their molecular interactions. The resulting multifunctional peptides show potential for functional food development targeting diabetes and related metabolic conditions.

papers.title: Ginsenoside Rb1 From the Functional Food Panax ginseng Suppresses Pancreatic Cancer Progression via Macrophage Reprogramming Through the PI3K-AKT Pathway.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly malignant gastrointestinal tumor, and its nutritional intervention strategies remain relatively limited. Ginseng, a representative medicinal herb officially included in China's "Food and Medicinal Same Origin" catalogue, is widely used in tea beverages, soups, and functional foods. Its active component, ginsenoside Rb1 (GRB1), derived from the medicine-food homology plant Panax ginseng, has been reported to possess antitumor and immunomodulatory effects, but its role in the PDAC tumor microenvironment remains unclear. This study aims to scree
papers.summary: This study investigates whether ginsenoside Rb1, a compound from the functional food Panax ginseng, can suppress pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) progression by reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages. The authors propose that GRB1 acts through the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway to modulate the tumor microenvironment and inhibit cancer growth.

papers.title: SMartini: automated small molecule parametrization for Martini 3 force field.
papers.abstract: We present SMartini, an automated pipeline for deriving Martini 3 coarse-grained force-field parameters for arbitrary small molecules. Starting from a molecular structure or a SMILES string, the pipeline maps the all-atom molecule onto a coarse-grained bead representation and automatically fits both bonded and non-bonded parameters. Bonded parameters are obtained via Boltzmann inversion of atomistic molecular dynamics trajectories; successive rounds of coarse-grained simulation and distribution-matching updates then refine these estimates until the coarse-grained conformational ensemble reprod
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SMartini is an automated pipeline that derives Martini 3 coarse-grained force-field parameters for arbitrary small molecules starting from a structure or SMILES string. It maps all-atom molecules onto coarse-grained beads and fits bonded parameters via Boltzmann inversion of atomistic MD trajectories, then iteratively refines them through coarse-grained simulation and distribution matching. This lowers the barrier to simulating small molecules in the popular Martini 3 framework.

papers.title: Systematic exploration of predicted quaternary structures within pandemic-relevant viral proteomes.
papers.abstract: Mechanistic understanding of viral protein-protein interactions enables global health security and pandemic preparedness, yet experimental characterisation remains difficult, costly, and often restricted to specialised laboratories. Here, we describe an in silico campaign using AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold-Multimer to predict monomers and dimer structures within 2,812 viral proteomes from 23 viral families relevant to human health. We report high-confidence predicted structures of 5,279 hetero-, and 2,749 homo-dimers. Structural clustering of interfaces reduces the set fivefold to 1,598 consolidat
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold-Multimer to predict monomer and dimer structures across 2,812 viral proteomes from 23 human-relevant viral families, generating high-confidence models for 5,279 heterodimers and 2,749 homodimers. Structural clustering of interfaces condensed the set to 1,598 consolidated interface groups, providing a large-scale resource for studying viral protein-protein interactions relevant to pandemic preparedness.

papers.title: UHPLC/MS-MS Profiling, Antioxidant and Antimicrobial Properties of Atriplex halimus L. and Marrubium deserti De Noé Extracts: In Vitro and In Silico.
papers.abstract: This study aims to evaluate the chemical composition and both in vitro and in silico antioxidant and antimicrobial activities of Atriplex halimus L. and Marrubium deserti De Noé, collected from Algeria. UHPLC‑MS/MS analysis revealed that the major compounds in the tested extracts are protocatechuic aldehyde, caffeic acid, cynaroside, and cosmosiin. The data demonstrated that the dichloromethane fraction was richer in polyphenols and flavonoids than the aqueous fraction. The extracts exhibited greater antioxidant capacity against ABTS compared to DPPH and FRAP assays. Antimicrobial activity was
papers.summary: This study profiles the chemical composition of Atriplex halimus and Marrubium deserti extracts using UHPLC-MS/MS, identifying major polyphenolic compounds such as protocatechuic aldehyde, caffeic acid, cynaroside, and cosmosiin. The dichloromethane fractions were richer in polyphenols and flavonoids and showed stronger antioxidant activity against ABTS than DPPH or FRAP, along with antimicrobial effects supported by in silico analyses.

papers.title: Green Extraction of Phenolic Compounds From Pistacia lentiscus Leaves Coupled With LC-MS Characterization and Structure-Based Enzyme Inhibition Analysis.
papers.abstract: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and urease are critical enzymes involved in various pathological conditions associated with cellular and tissue damage. Natural products are increasingly explored as safer alternatives to synthetic inhibitors. This study evaluates the phytochemical composition and enzyme inhibitory potential of Pistacia lentiscus leaves using a green extraction approach. Bioactive compounds were extracted via lactic acid-assisted ultrasound, and the crude extract was characterized for total phenolics, flavonoids, LC-MS profile, and in vitro inhibition of acetylcholinesterase and ure
papers.summary: This study uses a green extraction method (lactic acid-assisted ultrasound) to obtain phenolic compounds from Pistacia lentiscus leaves, characterizes them via LC-MS, and tests their ability to inhibit acetylcholinesterase and urease enzymes. The work highlights the potential of natural plant extracts as safer alternatives to synthetic enzyme inhibitors for conditions involving cellular damage.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products, a promising but underexplored anticancer target. The integrated computational approach aims to prioritize marine compounds as potential PIM-1 inhibitors for further development.

papers.title: Trypsinogen Pro-Region as a Molecular Scaffold for the Design of Competitive Peptide Inhibitors of Trypsin-Like Proteases.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max L. Merrill) productivity is severely impacted by the velvetbean caterpillar Anticarsia gemmatalis Hübner, 1818 (Lepidoptera: Erebidae), a major defoliating pest in soybean-producing regions. Current management strategies rely heavily on chemical insecticides, which are associated with environmental risks and the development of resistance. Protease inhibitors have emerged as a promising alternative, as protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae is primarily mediated by trypsin-like serine proteases. In this context, the rational design of short inhibitory peptides represents
papers.journal: Archives of insect biochemistry and physiology
papers.summary: This paper explores using the pro-region of trypsinogen as a molecular scaffold to rationally design short competitive peptide inhibitors targeting trypsin-like serine proteases in the velvetbean caterpillar, a major soybean pest. The approach aims to provide an environmentally friendly alternative to chemical insecticides by disrupting protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae.

papers.title: Multidimensional molecular profiling reveals decidual and circulating NK cell dynamics in early and late pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Human pregnancy presents a unique physiological state that allows for growth of an antigenically dissimilar foetus. The immune system plays a key role in establishing and maintaining successful pregnancy, yet detailed understanding of immunological responses in pregnancy is lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses multidimensional molecular profiling to characterize natural killer (NK) cell populations in the decidua (uterine lining) and peripheral blood across early and late pregnancy. It reveals dynamic changes in NK cell phenotypes and functions that likely support fetal tolerance and immune adaptation during gestation. The findings provide a detailed immune atlas of pregnancy-relevant NK cells, highlighting their potential roles in maintaining successful pregnancy.

papers.title: KRT14 activated by transcription factor E2F1 promotes bladder cancer progression.
papers.abstract: Bladder cancer is one of the most common cancers in the world, and its high malignancy threatens human health. Therefore, it is vital to explore new therapeutic targets for the early diagnosis and prognosis evaluation of bladder cancer. Keratin 14 (KRT14) is the oncogene of numerous cancers, but its role and mechanism in bladder cancer are not completely clear. The present study aimed to assess the molecular mechanism of KRT14 in bladder cancer. Bioinformatics analyses were performed to screen KRT14 as an oncogene in bladder cancer. Moreover, KRT14 small interfering RNA and KRT14 overexpressio
papers.summary: This study identifies KRT14 as an oncogene in bladder cancer, showing that the transcription factor E2F1 activates its expression to drive tumor progression. Knockdown and overexpression experiments suggest KRT14 promotes bladder cancer malignancy, highlighting it as a potential diagnostic or therapeutic target.

papers.title: Structure-based discovery of a novel Granzyme A (GZMA) inhibitor for autism spectrum disorder through integrative transcriptomics, virtual screening, and long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Granzyme A (GZMA) is a trypsin-like serine protease expressed in cytotoxic lymphocytes that cleaves gasdermin B (GSDMB) to release a pore-forming N-terminal fragment, thereby inducing pyroptosis, a lytic and pro-inflammatory form of programmed cell death. This pathway has been implicated in immune dysregulation reported in a subset of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In this study, we reanalyzed the peripheral blood transcriptome dataset GSE26415 using an integrative computational framework comprising outlier-aware quality control, differential expression analysis, functional e
papers.summary: This study identifies Granzyme A (GZMA) as a potential therapeutic target for autism spectrum disorder by reanalyzing peripheral blood transcriptome data and linking it to immune dysregulation via the GZMA-GSDMB pyroptosis pathway. Using virtual screening and long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations, the authors discover a novel small-molecule GZMA inhibitor as a candidate drug. The work integrates transcriptomics with structure-based drug discovery to propose a new treatment avenue for a subset of ASD patients.

papers.title: Designing a multi-epitope vaccine against La Crosse virus using immunoinformatics approach.
papers.abstract: La Crosse virus (LACV) is a mosquito-borne Orthobunyavirus responsible for pediatric encephalitis, with no currently approved vaccine or targeted antiviral therapy. This study aimed to design a multi-epitope subunit vaccine targeting the conserved nucleoprotein of LACV using an integrated immunoinformatics approach. The nucleoprotein exhibited strong antigenicity and favorable physicochemical properties, including stability and hydrophilicity. Highly conserved CTL, HTL, and B-cell epitopes were initially predicted, from which high-affinity, non-allergenic, and non-toxic epitopes were selected.
papers.summary: This study uses immunoinformatics to design a multi-epitope subunit vaccine against La Crosse virus, a mosquito-borne pathogen causing pediatric encephalitis with no approved vaccine. By targeting the conserved nucleoprotein, the authors predicted and selected highly conserved, antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic CTL, HTL, and B-cell epitopes for vaccine construction. The work provides an in silico vaccine candidate that requires further experimental validation.

papers.title: Selective behavioral and prefrontal transcriptomic correlates of acute clozapine exposure in socially isolated mice.
papers.abstract: Clozapine is an effective antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, but acute molecular responses to clozapine remain incompletely characterized. Social isolation rearing produces schizophrenia-relevant behavioral abnormalities and permits joint evaluation of housing and drug exposure.
papers.summary: This study examines how acute clozapine exposure affects behavior and prefrontal cortex gene expression in mice raised in social isolation, a model for schizophrenia-relevant abnormalities. The authors identify selective behavioral and transcriptomic changes that depend on both housing condition and drug exposure, suggesting that social environment shapes molecular responses to antipsychotic treatment.

papers.title: Metabolite profiling and molecular dynamics-based in silico evaluation of methanolic leaf extracts of Stevia rebaudiana Bertoni against α-amylase and DPP-IV.
papers.abstract: Stevia rebaudiana Bertoni is a natural sweetener with reported antidiabetic properties; however, the molecular basis underlying the interactions of its major phytochemicals with key glycaemic-regulating enzymes remains insufficiently understood. The present study employed an integrated in silico workflow to evaluate the antidiabetic potential of selected steviol-derived phytochemicals against human pancreatic α-amylase and dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV). Methanolic leaf extracts were profiled by GC-MS, and steviol, together with the principal steviol glycosides (stevioside, rebaudioside A, a
papers.summary: This study profiled the phytochemicals in methanolic leaf extracts of Stevia rebaudiana using GC-MS and then used molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate how steviol and its glycosides (stevioside, rebaudioside A) interact with the antidiabetic targets α-amylase and DPP-IV. The work provides in silico evidence for the molecular basis of Stevia's reported antidiabetic effects, identifying potential binding interactions with these glycaemic-regulating enzymes.

papers.title: A comparative analysis of graph neural networks and classical machine learning for carbapenem-resistance prediction and genomic interpretation in Acinetobacter baumannii.
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii is a hospital-associated pathogen linked to high mortality and limited treatment options. Although many resistance determinants have been identified, how they organize into coordinated systems remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study compares graph neural networks against classical machine learning methods for predicting carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, a major hospital pathogen. It also explores how these models can aid genomic interpretation by revealing how resistance determinants organize into coordinated systems. The work helps clarify which modeling approaches best capture the complex genetic architecture underlying resistance.

papers.title: Integrated computation-guided thermostabilization of the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener.
papers.abstract: Thermostability limits the use of sweet proteins as sugar substitutes in thermally processed foods. Here, we report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a recently identified fungal sweet protein with low intrinsic stability. We determined the HTS crystal structure and used it to guide subsequent computational analyses. Rosetta and ThermoMPNN evaluated candidate substitutions from complementary physics-based and deep-learning-based perspectives, and the selected single-mutant library was experimentally characterized. The resulting melti
papers.summary: This study reports a computation-guided workflow to improve the thermostability of Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a fungal sweet protein with poor intrinsic stability that limits its use in processed foods. The authors solved the HTS crystal structure and combined Rosetta (physics-based) and ThermoMPNN (deep-learning) predictions to design single-mutant variants, which were experimentally validated for improved melting temperatures. The work demonstrates an integrated structure-guided protein engineering strategy for stabilizing food-relevant proteins.

papers.title: Molecular biophysics of viral proteins: From mechanistic insights to microbiological and clinical applications.
papers.abstract: Viral proteins are dynamic molecular machines that couple molecular-scale events to microbiological phenotypes, including host-cell tropism, entry efficiency, environmental persistence, strain-specific immune escape, and antiviral resistance. In this review, we critically evaluated how experimental, computational, and biochemical approaches define these links and support clinical translation. We organized the evidence around four key observables: Structure, dynamics, mechanics, and thermodynamics. We then assessed which conclusions remained robust across methods and viral families. Nuclear mag
papers.summary: This review examines how experimental, computational, and biochemical methods reveal the structure, dynamics, mechanics, and thermodynamics of viral proteins, linking molecular-scale behavior to phenotypes like host tropism, immune escape, and antiviral resistance. It assesses which conclusions hold across different methods and viral families, and discusses how these mechanistic insights can inform clinical applications.

papers.title: Tau protein in Parkinson's disease: advances in phosphoproteomics and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Tau dysregulation, particularly abnormal phosphorylation, is increasingly implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD) and in the pathogenic interaction between Tau and α-synuclein. This review proposes an integrated PD-focused workflow connecting phosphoproteomic discovery, structural modeling, computational drug discovery, and experimental validation. Phosphoproteomic analyses of post-mortem brain tissue, biofluids, and patient-derived dopaminergic neuronal models can identify candidate Tau phosphosignatures associated with vulnerable brain regions, α-synuclein pathology, genetic background, or cl
papers.summary: This review proposes an integrated workflow for studying Tau dysregulation in Parkinson's disease, combining phosphoproteomic discovery from patient tissue and models with structural modeling and computational drug discovery. It highlights how abnormal Tau phosphorylation and its interaction with α-synuclein may contribute to PD pathogenesis, and outlines a path from phosphosignature discovery to experimental validation.

papers.title: Shared immune perturbations in hepatocellular carcinoma-depression comorbidity and synergistic immunotherapeutic effects of fluoxetine combined with anti-PD-1.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) often coexists with depression, elevating patient mortality by 39%. The tryptophan metabolic axis bridges tumor and neuropsychiatric immune dysfunction, yet the immunometabolic crosstalk underlying HCC-depression comorbidity remains poorly defined, and reliable combinatorial immunotherapies are absent.
papers.summary: This study investigates the shared immune and metabolic perturbations linking hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and depression, focusing on the tryptophan metabolic axis as a bridge between tumor and neuropsychiatric immune dysfunction. The authors report that combining the antidepressant fluoxetine with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy produces synergistic anti-tumor effects, suggesting a potential combinatorial treatment strategy for patients with HCC-depression comorbidity.

papers.title: Insights into osteoporosis triggered by common antiepileptic drugs via network toxicology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Antiepileptic drugs (AEDs), first-line treatments for epilepsy and related seizure disorders, are increasingly recognized as important risk factors for osteoporosis. However, the molecular mechanisms and specific targets underlying AED-induced bone loss remain largely unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology combined with molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how common antiepileptic drugs may trigger osteoporosis. The authors identify potential molecular targets and pathways linking AED exposure to bone loss, offering mechanistic hypotheses for this known clinical side effect.

papers.title: Reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics-driven design of a multiepitope vaccine candidate against Renibacterium salmoninarum.
papers.abstract: Renibacterium salmoninarum, the etiological agent of bacterial kidney disease (BKD), remains a major challenge for salmonid aquaculture due to its intracellular lifestyle, chronic infection pattern, and the limited efficacy of current control strategies. In this study, a multiepitope vaccine candidate against Renibacterium salmoninarum was designed using reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics approaches. Conserved antigenic proteins shared among three bacterial strains were identified through a systematic screening pipeline that included virulence prediction, essentiality analysis, antigeni
papers.summary: This study used reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics to design a multiepitope vaccine candidate against Renibacterium salmoninarum, the bacterium causing bacterial kidney disease in salmonids. The authors screened conserved antigenic proteins across three bacterial strains, applying virulence prediction, essentiality analysis, and antigenicity assessment to identify promising epitopes for vaccine construction. The work provides an in silico vaccine design that could address the limited efficacy of current control strategies for this economically important aquaculture pathogen.

papers.title: Multimodal profiling uncovers an aging-associated ETS1-MYO1B vascular niche responsive to ipragliflozin.
papers.abstract: Tissue aging involves complex changes in vascular, immune, and stromal compartments that collectively reshape the local tissue ecosystem and may contribute to age-related diseases, including cancer, fibrotic diseases, and cardiovascular disease. However, it remains unclear whether reproducible, cell-specific vascular niche states emerge during aging and whether these states can be therapeutically targeted.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Using multimodal profiling, this study identifies a reproducible aging-associated vascular niche state defined by ETS1-MYO1B expression that emerges across tissues during aging. The authors show this niche can be therapeutically modulated by ipragliflozin, suggesting a targetable vascular component of tissue aging.

papers.title: Integrated computational investigation of Glycosmis pentaphylla-derived compounds against major venom proteins of Daboia russelii.
papers.abstract: Snakebite envenomation remains a significant neglected tropical disease, particularly in South Asia, where Daboia russelii (Russell's viper) causes substantial morbidity and mortality. Current antivenom therapy is limited by poor efficacy against local tissue damage, high production costs, restricted toxin specificity, and adverse immune reactions, highlighting the need for alternative or adjunct therapeutic strategies. Using an integrated computational and experimental approach, phytocompounds identified from Glycosmis pentaphylla leaf extracts were evaluated as potential inhibitors of major
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and simulation alongside experimental assays to test phytocompounds from Glycosmis pentaphylla leaves as inhibitors of major venom proteins from Russell's viper (Daboia russelii). The work aims to identify plant-derived molecules that could serve as alternatives or adjuncts to conventional antivenom, which struggles with local tissue damage and high costs. It represents an early-stage drug-discovery effort targeting a neglected tropical disease.

papers.title: Discovery of sunflower-derived umami peptides via machine learning and molecular dynamics simulation of their interactions with the T1R1/T1R3 receptor.
papers.abstract: Umami recognition relies on T1R1/T1R3 binding with umami peptides, but the interaction mechanisms remain unclear. This study aims to reveal the taste mechanisms of four potential umami peptides at both sensory and molecular levels.
papers.summary: This study identifies four potential umami peptides derived from sunflower and investigates how they bind to the T1R1/T1R3 umami taste receptor. Using machine learning for peptide discovery combined with molecular dynamics simulations, the authors characterize the molecular interactions underlying umami perception. The work links computational prediction with mechanistic insight into taste receptor binding.

papers.title: Underpinning hierarchical anisotropic structure formation in soy protein high-moisture extrudates by Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
papers.abstract: Plant-based meat alternatives are fibrous anisotropic food protein products that mimic the texture and palatability of animal-based foods. The main industrially scalable production technique for manufacturing such structured protein materials is high-moisture extrusion, which involves the thermo-mechanical processing, and subsequent cooling, of a hot protein melt in the presence of shear and temperature gradients. Yet, the complex mechanisms governing fibrous structure formation in plant-protein extrudates are poorly characterised, in turn limiting the rational design and optimisation of the e
papers.summary: This study uses Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) to visualize how hierarchical anisotropic fibrous structures form in soy protein high-moisture extrudates during thermo-mechanical processing. The work provides new insights into the mechanisms of fiber formation under shear and temperature gradients, which could enable more rational design of plant-based meat alternatives.

papers.title: Nanozymes in Tumor Microenvironment Modulation for Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central regulatory role in malignant tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, and its complexity and dynamic heterogeneity markedly limit the efficacy of current treatment strategies. Therefore, the development of novel functional materials capable of effectively remodeling the TME and alleviating immunosuppression and therapeutic tolerance has become an important research direction in cancer therapy. In recent years, nanozymes, as a class of nanomaterials with enzyme-mimicking catalytic activity, have shown broad potential in TME intervention and
papers.summary: This review discusses nanozymes—nanomaterials that mimic enzyme catalytic activity—as tools to remodel the tumor microenvironment and overcome immunosuppression and therapeutic resistance in cancer. It highlights how these materials could intervene in the complex, dynamic TME to improve treatment outcomes.

papers.title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies ethyl rosmarinate as a SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate for bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: SLC1A6 remains poorly characterized in bladder cancer. This study investigated its expression pattern, clinical relevance, cellular localization, functional implications, and potential pharmacological modulation.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the poorly understood glutamate transporter SLC1A6 in bladder cancer, examining its expression, clinical relevance, and cellular localization. Using structure-based virtual screening, the authors identify ethyl rosmarinate as a potential SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate for bladder cancer.
